text: Abigail gripped the polished brass railing of the luxury liner as it cut through the Pacific, heading toward the bustling metropolis of Neo-Tokyo. It was 2084, and she was leaving behind the rigid, algorithmic constraints of her traditional life in a rural data-farm for the promise of anonymity and adventure in the Free Zones. She clutched her small, battered data-drive that contained all her worldly possessions, her heart racing with both fear and excitement. Tell me what a book is primarily made of.
